# Recorded dsh session store (hand-authored)

A fake `$DSH_HOME` for `adg/dsh.py`'s parser: point `DSH_HOME` at this
directory and the reader finds `sessions/` under it exactly as it would under
`~/.dsh`. Three project directories, matching the layout
`dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` computes:
`<root>/<projectKey(cwd)>/<sessionId>/session.jsonl[.zstd]`.

**These files were written by hand from the type declarations shipped inside
`@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.0-rc.6`, not captured from a run.** There is no DeepSeek
API key in this environment, so no session has ever been observed on disk. Every
field here traces to a declaration — `SessionEventMap`, `TokenUsage`,
`TurnEndReason`, `LlmFailure`, `MessageSource` — and none to a guess about how
the harness behaves. `orchestrator/docs/dsh-adapter-notes.md` records the
verified/assumed split point by point; the layout and the schema are verified,
"a real run writes one of these" is not.

| Directory | What it exercises |
|---|---|
| `--tmp-proj--/s-01` | The ordinary case: usage summed over `assistant/message`, both `user/message` source kinds (`user` and `plugin`), and a packed `text-chunks` row — which `packChunks: true` writes by default and which is **not** a `SessionEvent`, so a reader must skip it rather than choke. |
| `--tmp-walled--/s-02` | A provider wall as `turn/end` → `reason.kind: "error"` → `LlmFailure`, carrying `code`, `status` and `providerRetryAfterMs`. Its `user/message` deliberately contains "429" and "rate_limit" as the AGENT's own words, so a test can prove the wall is read from the structured failure and not from the prose beside it. Ends in an unknown event type and a torn line, both of which a live append-only log routinely has. |
| `--tmp-zstd--/s-03` | The default artifact this reader cannot open. Seven bytes of a Zstandard frame header — enough to be found and refused by name, and no decoder is attempted. |

Nothing here is regenerated by a script. If dsh's schema moves, these files are
edited by a human who has read the new declarations, for the same reason
`provider-messages.json` is not auto-ingested: a fixture that pins behaviour
must not be written by the behaviour it pins.
